sentences.text: The genus Agkistracanthus contains only one known species, A. mitgelensis. Knowledge of this animal comes mostly from isolated and fragmentary fossils, including fin spines and parts of the skull and jaws.
It belongs to the family Myriacanthidae and is classified in the class Chondrichthyes, a group of cartilaginous fish.
The genus Agkistracanthus was described by Duffin and Furrer in 1981.
Agkistracanthus lived during the Rhaetian to Hettangian epochs, covering the transition from the Triassic to the Jurassic period. This span covers the time between 205.7 and 199.5 million years ago.
Fossils of Agkistracanthus have been found in Switzerland, Austria, and Britain.
